how: A member begins a picture and invites others to join using an anchor coordinate and reference image.
Calls recruit volunteers to start, finish and maintain a specific shared picture.
Starting and calling coincide in one invitation, supporting their connection without measuring a separate interval.
Recruitment is followed by reported commitment and construction, although the placing caused by each call cannot be measured.
A specific invitation to help receives a bare acceptance asking for nothing back.
The direct invitation and bare answer support the proposed acceptance form without making it obligatory for every participant.
Limited manpower and remaining time lead the organiser to prioritise finishing the existing head over additional figures.
After one project is erased, a participant can transfer effort to another member's surviving build instead of relocating the original picture.

statement: Redirecting effort from a lost project into an existing shared build
how: Destruction redirects a participant into an existing shared project, preserving participation without rebuilding the lost picture.
The switch names destruction as its reason, while the separate manpower warning cannot establish that shortage caused relocation.
Participants choose additions and postpone expansion while weighing manpower, time and the current picture.
Task invitations and a manpower metaphor do not settle whether formal order was decided in the unseen chat.
Builders report outlining parts for others to fill while public updates describe the growing body.
Coordinates locate the work and a common reference guides details while helping prevent builders from deleting one another's changes.
A reference may accompany the first proposal and remain contested during construction rather than emerge only after design discussion has settled.
Live questions and coordination move to chat while public thread updates continue, dividing reporting across venues.

statement: Splitting live coordination between chat and public updates
how: Repeated public edits become inadequate, prompting faster chat coordination while public recruitment and reports remain available.
Builders repair changed pixels, prioritise upkeep and renew calls for help even after the picture is publicly celebrated.
Construction creates a picture requiring defence while growth and upkeep continue together.
A builder interprets erased details as intended work mistaken for damage and changes tasks in response.
Repair requires knowing the intended reference because well-meant restoration can erase planned construction.
The organiser reports arranging a defence script and directs absent or sleeping members to installation instructions.
The organiser explicitly connects automated defence to upkeep demands, although realised bot performance remains unresolved.
The organiser expects automated upkeep to release manual effort for construction, without demonstrating the resulting increase in progress.
Neighbours discuss competing space claims and arrive at a reported arrangement keeping both drawings.
Expansion is limited to avoid neighbouring creations and the organiser reports an agreement preventing overlap.
The organiser thanks a neighbour for bot help without documenting a reciprocal price for that assistance.
Border negotiation can address the room's prospective encroachment on neighbours rather than respond only to neighbours eroding its own work.
An agreement establishes intended restraint without demonstrating that every unaffiliated painter follows it.
An organiser disclaims control over most painters while seeking compromise, showing limited practical reach without an explicit rejection of representative legitimacy.
Compliance problems surface during negotiation before settlement, so the proposed mechanism must not require an agreement already made in the room's name.
A bilateral no-overlap agreement and bot assistance do not establish coalition membership or reciprocal defence obligations.
The record reports incoming encroachment and limited control over painters but does not establish a room-authorised attack call.
Contrasting flag fights with defending a character does not establish sustained rivalry talk or taunting between rooms.
Recruitment is visible but its proposed conversion into an attack call is unobserved.
Members celebrate visibility, thank helpers, claim participation and reflect on coming together.
Celebration can follow visibility before completion, so a report that the work is finished is not a necessary local trigger.
Post-event comments recount survival under interference and appraise the resulting picture.
Celebration and retrospective appraisal coexist without demonstrating that the former caused a separate preservation decision.

statement: Finding the room through its visible canvas work
how: A viewer reports discovering the subreddit through its picture, establishing one return of visibility without measuring lasting recruitment.
Minor disagreement over the finished picture's perfection does not establish a contest over cleanup, retained versions or historical fidelity.
Reflection on community togetherness supplies no observed decision to carry the work into a new canvas or enduring arrangement.
Retrospective appraisal does not show a subsequent decision about carrying the temporary effort forward.
The move to chat is explained by update speed and does not establish host moderation or containment of canvas talk.
Calls and venue changes occur without an observed moderation boundary arising in response to recruitment.
A joke about the drawing's haircut does not establish a host April Fools frame making the canvas calls potentially fake.
A haircut joke brings character lore into appraisal of the shared outline without naming an enemy or directing an attack.
The contrast between flag fights and character defence does not establish a pre-existing tie naming an attack target.
